 Orderly security operations observed at NAIA amid ASEAN Summit hosting: OTS
 by 
 Cristina Arayata
 Nov 16, 2026
 5:12 PM GMT+8
 HEIGHTENED SECURITY .  Office for Transportation Security (OTS) Administrator Gilbert Cruz (3rd from left) leads the inspection and checking of security equipment at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) on Monday (Nov. 16, 2026). The inspections seek to ensure the safe, orderly, and smooth movement of ASEAN delegates.  (Photo courtesy of OTS) 
 MANILA – Security operations at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) remain generally stable and orderly amid the country's hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, the head of the Office for Transportation Security (OTS) said on Monday.
 Most of the global leaders and delegates who have arrived starting last Friday landed via the main gateway, and some are still expected to come.
 "The OTS, coordination with airport authorities and law enforcement agencies, continues to implement established security screening standards across all security screening checkpoints, and maintain heightened vigilance to ensure the safety and security of the traveling public," OTS Administrator Gilbert Cruz told the Philippine News Agency in an interview.
 Cruz led the inspection of NAIA terminals on Monday to monitor the situation and address any potential security concerns or issues.
 "The OTS is prepared to sustain its security operations and ensure the continuous implementation of established screening procedures," he said.
 Cruz said the OTS ensures that necessary personnel and operational resources are in place to respond appropriately to any developments.
 "Our priority is to maintain a high level of security readiness throughout the ASEAN Summit," he added.
 Meanwhile, Cruz appealed to passengers to remain calm, vigilant, and cooperative with airport security personnel.
 They are also urged to allot sufficient time for airport check-in and security screening, and immediately report any suspicious activity or unattended items to authorities.
 "We ask for everyone's understanding and cooperation as these measures are in place to protect all passengers," Cruz said.   (PNA)
